editionData.title: Beijing expands purge of top generals; Sliman Mansour has died. His art became a symbol of Palestinian resilience.
editionData.description: Global headlines: Beijing expands purge of top generals (President Xi Jinping is targeting officers affiliated with previously ousted leaders, analysts say, even as Beijing seeks to project power across the Indo-Pacific); Sliman Mansour has died. His art became a symbol of Palestinian resilience. (For more than 50 years, he explored Palestinian life and history in his paintings. His work became increasingly political after he spent time in jail); and Ka-nyet! Kanye West concerts canceled in Russia. (Two sold-out shows in St. Petersburg were scrapped, highlighting wartime ambivalence about Western culture and the rapper’s past antisemitic remarks). Markets leaned higher, with 4 of 7 tracked indexes up; Euronext 100 Index up 0.75% was the largest move. Benchmarks tracked: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, Euronext 100 Index, and Public Joint-Stock Company Moscow Exchange MICEX-RTS plus 3 more indexes. Hacker News: Bug Blindness (I used to wonder why I see so many more bugs than most people. I easily observe hundreds to thousands of bugs per week and nothing seems...); Hy4 preview (Tencent has released and open-sourced Tencent Hy4 preview, a next-generation large language model with 770B total parameters and 49B...); and California lawmakers unanimously pass Linux exemption from age-verification law (AB 1856 excludes open-source operating systems from the upcoming Digital Age Assurance Act). Product Hunt features Hyperfocus (Planner that turns goals into daily progress), Maritime (Dedicated computers for AI agents, starting at $1/month), and Topview Motion Studio (Create launch videos without touching After Effects).
editionData.author: Sony Mathew

headlines.summary: The plan involves the United States taking more direct control over Venezuelan reserves as crime and steep logistical challenges discourage private investors.

headlines.title: Venezuela says it retains ‘sovereignty’ following US oil deal
headlines.summary: Under the deal, $19 from every barrel of oil sold to the US will flow to Caracas, interim President Rodriguez says.

headlines.title: US deports relative of Afghans who aided military to Africa
headlines.summary: Afghan national granted protection in the US is one of dozens of people deported to war-torn Central African Republic.

headlines.title: AI chatbots may be better than search engines in guarding against foreign propaganda
headlines.summary: In a test, popular AI chatbots mostly debunked falsehoods spread by other countries and avoided uncritically spreading falsehoods better than search engines. AI summaries above search results fared worse.

headlines.summary: The final vote is expected to be extremely close, with ballot counting continuing through the night.

headlines.summary: The controversial commentator, who criticized feminism and Islam, was an enthusiastic supporter of President Trump's immigration crackdown. ICE says he was an "illegal alien."

headlines.summary: The deadly strike comes amid 72 hours of near constant drone strikes across Ukraine, severely disrupting daily life.

headlines.summary: Nepal officials say the death toll has continues to rise in Wednesday's floods that washed away communities in Nepal and Tibet, which is held by China. About 2,500 people are missing in both areas.

headlines.title: 359 dead, 910 missing in Nepal's floods
headlines.summary: KATHMANDU -- Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction Management Authority said that as many as 359 bodies had been recovered from flood-hit areas by Thursday evening, with 910 people still missing.

headlines.title: China's 'grass tech' helps reap rich harvest in Fiji
headlines.summary: SUVA, Fiji — On a stretch of land once scarred by salt, rows of lush green grass now ripple in the Pacific breeze. Just a few years ago, little could grow here.

headlines.summary: Canada's new retaliatory tariffs will deepen the economic pain from its trade fight with the United States, with experts saying both countries will bear the costs.

headlines.title: Moldova eyes expanding cooperation with China
headlines.summary: This year marks the 35th anniversary of the Republic of Moldova's independence, offering an opportunity to reflect on the steady development of Moldova-China relations over the past three and a half decades and to look ahead with confidence to the next stage of the bilateral partnership, said the Moldovan ambassador to China.

headlines.summary: India and China are set to establish two new border meeting points, locations yet to be announced, following recent high-level talks.

headlines.title: BJP brainstorming on Gen Z outreach concludes cohort is not ‘homogenous’
headlines.summary: BJP's Gen Z outreach strategy meeting highlights the need for differentiated engagement and broader terms like "youth" for better connection.

headlines.title: One dead, several injured, in Swiss shooting incident, police say
headlines.summary: A shooting in northern Switzerland ‌has killed one person and injured at least five, some of them seriously, ​local police said on Sunday.

headlines.title: Nepal-Tibet death toll 750 from Himalayan flood, 3,000 missing
headlines.summary: Rescuers in Nepal and China raced on Sunday to find thousands of people ​missing after a glacier collapse unleashed a catastrophic mudslide across the Himalayas, as they faced challenging weather conditions and rising water levels.

headlines.title: South Korea names veteran technocrat Lee Hyoung-il as new finance chief in cabinet reshuffle
headlines.summary: South Korea unveiled a major cabinet reshuffle on Sunday, naming First Vice Finance Minister ​Lee Hyoung-il as the new deputy prime minister ‌and minister of economy and finance.

headlines.title: Finland's Stubb tells German newspaper Russia unlikely to risk attack on NATO
headlines.summary: Finland's President Alexander Stubb said he did not believe Russia would risk an attack against a NATO country, telling Germany's Bild newspaper it would "make ​no sense" to test the resolve of the alliance.

hackerNews.title: Bug Blindness
hackerNews.summary: I used to wonder why I see so many more bugs than most people. I easily observe hundreds to thousands of bugs per week and nothing seems to work , but most people I talk to don't see anything like this . For a long time, I thought this had something to do with how I use computers but, over time, I've realized that it's mostly that people are hitting the same bugs and don't notice.
